projects.user: Manufacturing and procurement engineers reviewing a multilevel BOM export before a material estimate.
projects.pain: Shared subassemblies and decimal quantities make spreadsheet multiplication easy to undercount; a missing leaf price should not silently look like a complete estimate.
projects.capability: Propagate exact demand through a multilevel CSV BOM, combine shared paths once at each part, and show leaf costs plus an edge-by-edge quantity ledger.
projects.acceptance: Shared diamond propagation yields 4.6 leaf units and an exact 11.5 subtotal for the synthetic two-unit root; missing prices withhold the total; cycles fail; deep chains do not require Python recursion.
projects.overlap: table-reconcile compares captured keyed tables; invoice-rounding-ledger allocates invoice/tax rounding; backup-chain-audit follows preservation ancestry. This project performs multilevel bill-of-material quantities and material cost aggregation from CSV.
projects.alternatives: InvenTree for managed inventory/BOM pricing; KiCost for electronics supplier-cost spreadsheets; KiBot for reproducible KiCad outputs; a hand-maintained spreadsheet for a small one-off estimate.
projects.notes: InvenTree already documents BOM pricing, cost ranges and broader stock/pricing workflows. KiCost already builds quantity-adjusted supplier/cost spreadsheets, including handmade CSVs. KiBot automates KiCad outputs. Our narrower user path is an explicit two-CSV material rollup without a server or supplier lookup, not a claimed missing competitor capability.

projects.user: Developers reducing a local SQLite bug reproduction to selected rows and their required parents.
projects.pain: Copying a few tables or rows naively can lose required parents, while exporting the whole source shares unrelated data and makes reproduction cumbersome.
projects.capability: Open a SQLite source read-only, follow declared parent primary-key foreign keys to a fixed point, and emit deterministic INSERTs with per-row inclusion evidence.
projects.acceptance: Selecting synthetic invoice100 includes exactly invoice100 and account1, excludes unrelated rows, and restores into an empty matching schema with no foreign-key violations. Composite keys, SQLite parent collation, cycles and BLOB/NUL-text round trips are tested; source bytes remain unchanged.
projects.overlap: sqlite-rehearsal rehearses migrations and sqlite-plan-witness explains query plans. This extracts row-level parent closure and executable INSERT fixtures from a real SQLite file.
projects.alternatives: Jailer for broad relational browsing/subsetting; Condenser for Postgres/MySQL; archived rdbms-subsetter as historical Python precedent. msg555/subsetter and DBSubsetter were also inspected as low-star alternatives and are not presented as widely adopted.
projects.notes: Jailer already supports referentially intact subsetting and multiple export formats across JDBC databases, including SQLite. Condenser is a config-driven Postgres/MySQL tool, not a SQLite adapter. 18F rdbms-subsetter is archived (last push2017), so its maintenance is historical. Our fixed local SQLite primary-key closure is deliberately smaller, not a feature-absence or reliability-superiority claim.

projects.user: Localization engineers checking a text corpus against locally available OpenType/TrueType fonts before packaging a fallback set.
projects.pain: A font family name does not prove nominal coverage for a corpus, and coverage union can conceal missing code points or inconsistent cmap choice.
projects.capability: Parse real standalone SFNT cmap format4/12 mappings, report per-font corpus gaps and choose a deterministic greedy fallback order with code-point evidence.
projects.acceptance: Synthetic Latin/accent fonts cover ABé🙂 in a stable two-step plan; missing characters are explicit. Format4 delta/array and format12 non-BMP mappings, offsets, malformed tables and preferred unsupported encodings are tested. Two installed real TTF/OTF files match FontTools4.61.1 on65617 queried code points each.
projects.overlap: colortool/colourdist deal with colors, and no existing owned project inspected handles SFNT character maps or font-set corpus coverage.
projects.alternatives: FontForge for interactive font editing; FontTools for full font manipulation and scripting; FontBakery for extensive QA. These provide much broader format and validation support.
projects.notes: FontForge is a full font editor and converter. FontTools already manipulates cmap mappings and exposes a preferred Unicode cmap. FontBakery offers broad font QA checks, with Fontspector as a related Rust port. Our bounded corpus-and-fallback report is an explicit standalone workflow; it does not prove these tools lack an equivalent script or check.

projects.user: Outdoor-track analysts reviewing apparent stops and capture gaps before summarizing a GPX activity.
projects.pain: A long interval between nearby points can be a sampling gap rather than a recorded stop, and slow GPS drift or jumps can distort moving/stopped summaries.
projects.capability: Read actual GPX1.1 track segments and emit fixed-anchor dwell windows, separate gap/speed-jump evidence and raw versus accepted pair totals.
projects.acceptance: Synthetic three-point stationary run yields120 seconds, then ends before a moving point. Segments, gaps and speed jumps cannot manufacture a joined stop. Slow drift, dateline crossing, prefixes, timezone equivalence and malformed XML/times/coordinates are tested.
projects.overlap: geojson-delivery-contract validates geospatial delivery geometry and subtitle-timing-audit handles media timing. This parses GPX track segmentation and spatial/time dwell evidence.
projects.alternatives: GPXSee for desktop inspection, gpx.studio for interactive editing and gpxpy for Python GPX analysis. Broad GPX search also returned hardware firmware, galleries and activity homepages; those were outside the selected offline dwell-report workflow.
projects.notes: GPXSee is a broad GPS viewer/analyzer, gpx.studio edits GPX in the browser, and gpxpy already offers moving/stopped data methods. Current gpxpy issue/PR discussions include zero stopped-speed thresholds, stationary intervals and prefixed namespaces; our tests explicitly cover these edges without claiming a new feature competitors lack. A gpx.studio issue asks for summary data, but it is adjacent interest rather than a verified request for our tool.

projects.user: Operations engineers checking aggregate pool-to-task capacity compatibility in a single planning period.
projects.pain: Total capacity can equal total demand while eligibility restrictions still leave demand unmet; an allocation alone does not explain the unavoidable bottleneck.
projects.capability: Compute integer max flow for explicit pool/task links, report idle and unfilled units, and expose cut edges whose capacity certifies the achieved maximum.
projects.acceptance: Synthetic capacity8/demand8 with restricted compatibility fulfills6, leaves2 idle and2 unmet, and a cut of capacity6. Reverse residual rerouting and100 seeded two-pool/two-task networks match independently enumerated cut minima.
projects.overlap: task-queue is a queue implementation, grid-ops-arena simulates energy dispatch and value-density-lab scores product outcomes. This is a static aggregate bipartite capacity-allocation/cut certificate tool.
projects.alternatives: NetworkX for graph modeling, OR-Tools for combinatorial optimization and Pyomo for algebraic models/solver integration. A hand calculation can handle a tiny matrix but does not scale to all compatibility cuts.
projects.notes: NetworkX already provides flow/cut algorithms; OR-Tools includes max flow, assignment and richer optimization; Pyomo models broad optimization problems with solvers. Our original small implementation packages a specific inspectable pool/task workflow without runtime packages. It does not claim algorithmic novelty, faster performance or missing functionality in those systems.
